sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent infrastructure dominates today’s list: agent operations, memory, orchestration, and AI-native office software occupy four of the nine entries. Local media/voice software and systems-level portability add a second strong thread.

sections.title: paperclipai/paperclip
sections.description: The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work

sections.title: debpalash/VoiceStudio
sections.description: VoiceStudio is the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative — voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.

sections.title: rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch
sections.description: Learn it. Build it. Ship it for others.

sections.title: InfinityLoop1308/PipePipe
sections.description: An open-source Android app to let you browse YouTube and other services freely.

sections.title: mvschwarz/openrig
sections.description: Multi-agent harness that runs Claude Code and Codex together as one system

sections.title: dream-num/univer
sections.description: The Office Harness for AI Agents — Spreadsheets, Docs, Slides, Canvas, Relational Tables, and PDF in one runtime.

sections.title: willfaust/Madeira
sections.description: Run x86-64 Windows PC games on jailed iOS via FEX-Emu + Wine + DXMT

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content:
- **Agent infrastructure and productivity:** paperclip, hindsight, openrig, and univer show demand for operational tooling, durable memory, multi-agent coordination, and AI-native office primitives.
- **Local and open AI experiences:** VoiceStudio brings voice generation/transcription on-device, while PipePipe offers a freer media client.
- **Languages:** TypeScript leads with 4 of 9 repositories, followed by Python with 3; Shell and C appear once each.
- **Compilers and runtimes:** scriptc and Madeira represent lower-level execution and portability beneath the AI-heavy layer.

sections.title: Notable Shifts
sections.content: The clearest shift is from end-user AI demos toward infrastructure that makes agents deployable: memory, work management, orchestration, and office integrations. At the same time, local-first software remains visible through VoiceStudio and PipePipe, while scriptc signals renewed interest in compiling TypeScript toward native execution.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today’s momentum is concentrated around the agent stack rather than a single model or application category. The strongest repositories pair AI with durable workflows or local execution, suggesting that practical integration, control, and portability are the themes attracting attention.
